title: Yeast growing in a flask
body: A student inoculated a few yeast cells into a flask containing a fixed volume of nutrient medium and kept it at a suitable temperature. Every two hours she estimated the population size. For the first few hours the numbers rose very slowly. Then the population increased rapidly, after which the rate of increase slowed down. From about the eighteenth hour onwards the population stayed nearly constant at about the same level, even though she continued to record it for many more hours. No fresh medium was added at any time.

title: The fig and its wasp
body: In many species of fig trees there is a tight one-to-one relationship with a pollinator species of wasp: a given fig species can be pollinated only by its partner wasp species. The female wasp enters the fig inflorescence looking for suitable sites to lay her eggs. While searching, she pollinates the flowers. She lays eggs inside the developing fruit, and her larvae feed on some of the developing seeds. The fig thus gets pollinated, and the wasp gets a safe place to lay eggs and food for its young.
